kinds.check: An automated test the organisation's own tooling runs at a Gate against what is in hand there — a working copy, the repository, a built bundle, a deployment or live state — with a pass or fail outcome. The Conformance Checks are the set of them.
kinds.configuration: A setting, or a single mandatory code path, that holds at a Gate or Standing without a separate test run — branch protection, a storage policy, an IAM binding, or a library path every runtime must call, such as the tool guard.
kinds.procedure: A documented step for a person or a governance agent, defined by the record it must produce.

enforcement.blocking: The thing at the Gate does not proceed, or the offending part is removed, as when a value is masked.
enforcement.reporting: A finding or event is recorded and the thing proceeds.
enforcement.attested: A person or agent confirms on a record that the condition held.

standing: a control that holds at all times and refuses every attempt that breaks it, whenever that attempt is made — an append-only grant, a write-once bucket, an identity-provider policy.

gates.name: Establish
gates.moment: A repository, project, environment, tenant, installation, supplier or person is created or onboarded.
gates.stops: The thing being created from coming into use, such as an installation's first release.

gates.name: Author
gates.moment: On the workstation, before a commit or a push leaves it.

gates.name: Pull request
gates.moment: A pull request against the release branch.

gates.name: Merge
gates.moment: A merge to the release branch: build, sign, publish and `dev` release.
gates.stops: Publication of the bundle and its `dev` release.

gates.name: Promote
gates.moment: The release pointer moves to `staging` or `prod`.

gates.name: Ingress
gates.moment: External content enters a run, or a request reaches a workload (the Standard, the Standard).

gates.name: Action
gates.moment: Before each model call, tool call or outbound network request (the Standard, the Standard).

gates.name: Response
gates.moment: Anything leaves: a tool result returning to the model, a model response to the caller, a workload's response, or a signal or Control Record leaving the run (the Standard, the Standard).
gates.stops: That output, which is withheld or masked.

gates.name: Operate
gates.moment: On a schedule or continuously, over live state.
gates.stops: Nothing directly. A failure is a finding, and an Incident where the Standard lists it; a control may revoke.

gates.name: Exit
gates.moment: A person, supplier, tenant, registry entry, agent or installation is retired.
gates.stops: Nothing. The Gate ensures that removal is complete and recorded; a failure is a finding against the exit.

controls.title: Every agent, installation and registry file matches its schema
Every agent's files follow the standard bundle layout, with nothing missing or extra
Every agent, skill, tool and server name follows the naming rules and is unique
Everything an agent references exists in a registry and is approved
Every skill follows the portable skill format and carries an approved licence
Every MCP server is pinned to an exact version, approved and fully declared
An agent's data classification can't exceed that of any model, service or source it uses
Every irreversible tool effect requires a person's review or approval, and its content is captured
Building the same agent bundle twice produces an identical result
Every agent run emits the required telemetry and nothing unpublished
A tool call outside the agent's allowlist is denied and recorded
An irreversible tool call is paused until a person reviews it
Message content is dropped from telemetry when content capture is off
Control records written by the control record writer match the control record schema
Every agent bundle passes its evaluation set before merge and before promotion

tier.minimum: A case for every shared skill whose tools carry a `write` or `irreversible` effect
tier.recommended: A case for every shared skill, which an installation may require

controls.title: A built agent bundle contains no secrets when it is published
Every installation's secrets exist, are readable only by its principal and are unexpired
No service an agent uses is overdue for re-assessment
Every agent file contains all six required sections
An injection attempt is refused, stripped or quarantined as the installation declares
Every tool and source passes a test that one tenant can't reach another's data
The integrations inventory matches the live grants, tokens and app installations on every host

tier.minimum: Reporting at `operate`
tier.recommended: Blocking at `pr`

controls.title: Workload endpoints reject unauthenticated, malformed and oversized requests
Every dependency version is at least 7 days old before it is adopted
MCP tool descriptions and skill text contain no hidden instructions
Every repository's project configuration matches the project baseline

tier.minimum: Attested — the files are generated from the baseline when the repository is created and their equality is attested at the quarterly access review (requirement 27.3)
tier.recommended: Blocking — the check compares them on every pull request

controls.title: Nothing passes a CI gate unless every blocking conformance check has passed
Secrets are blocked at commit, at push and in the built agent bundle
Every infrastructure plan passes the security rules before it is applied
All code passes format, lint and type checks before it merges

tier.minimum: The type checker runs in standard mode on the governance library (requirement 27.5); until the first workload that handles `confidential` data, the security rules of the baseline linter are the static analysis (requirement 27.8)
tier.recommended: Strict mode on every package, trigger: a second package in the repository; a static analysis tool as a required status check, a finding rated High or above blocking, trigger: the first workload that handles `confidential` data

controls.title: Every registry entry has a unique kind and id
Every cloud resource carries the required identifying labels
Every governed identifier is a UUID v7 created by the one approved generator
Every CI workflow uses minimal permissions and actions pinned to an exact version

tier.minimum: The organisation's Actions policy is set by hand at bootstrap and recorded in the bootstrap record
tier.recommended: The policy is declared as code and drift-checked (requirement 17.6)
tier.trigger: A second repository or a second person

controls.title: Infrastructure that differs from its code is detected every night
Unlabelled cloud resources are reported every night, and deleted in dev
Released components and images are checked every night for known vulnerabilities

tier.minimum: Until the first live release pointer, the Git host's dependency alerts are on for every repository and reviewed weekly (requirement 25.4)
tier.recommended: The nightly match of the Contract

controls.title: A registry entry is never deleted, and its status never moves backwards
Installations share a principal only when approved and at the same data classification

tier.minimum: Below `confidential`, installations of different tenants may share a principal at the same classification

controls.title: Every allowlisted host's domain is still held by its approved owner
Everything an installation uses processes data only in its tenant's permitted regions
No store holds a departed tenant's data once its exit period ends
Model provider usage matches what installations recorded, within 5%, checked every night
A tool call is denied if any one policy rule denies it
One end user can't reach another's data, tested before every promotion
Agents that decide about individuals pass fairness evaluations before merge and promotion
Models behind decisions about individuals have a fairness result recorded before approval
An agent starts each run within its tool cap and context budget

tier.minimum: Counts tokens as characters ÷ 4
tier.recommended: The model's own token counter

controls.title: Tools that run agent code against other systems declare their highest effect
Allowlisted tools with near-identical names or descriptions are flagged at review
Sandbox profiles allow no package index or code host
Each installation's resources are created and removed by one infrastructure module only
Every installation runs as its own single principal
Every new repository is generated from the project baseline
Every secret is readable by one installation's principal only
Files likely to hold secrets are kept out of every repository and image
Every install uses only the exact dependency versions in the committed lockfile

tier.minimum: The join reports a direct dependency with no `approved` entry in the `packages` registry (requirement 25.10; the Standard)
tier.recommended: It blocks the merge, and the rule extends to transitive dependencies
tier.trigger: The first approved release; the first `confidential` tenant

controls.title: Every person's workstation meets the security baseline

tier.minimum: Attested — the person attests each item of the baseline for each workstation (requirement 20.13)
tier.recommended: Device management reports each item of the baseline for every workstation, in place of the person's attestation

controls.title: The release branch accepts changes only through a reviewed pull request
Every change requires review by the owner of the code it touches
An agent's hooks call the tool guard and nothing else
Identity bindings are created only by the installation module; any other is refused
Package install scripts are disabled unless the package is on the allowlist

tier.minimum: A source build or lifecycle script not on the allowlist is reported (requirement 25.3)
tier.recommended: It fails the build

controls.title: Every pull request requires a person's approval before merging
Every commit on the release branch is signed, and traces to commits signed by a known person
Every build resolves and records each registry reference, refusing any not approved
Built agent bundles are stored under their content hash for tampering detection
Every agent bundle is signed by the trusted signer and verified before it loads
Every build records the attributes derived from the agent's name in its manifest
An agent's model is resolved from the models registry, never hard-coded
Every applied infrastructure plan and drift report is archived as a control record
The registry table is a copy of Git that only CI can write
A bill of materials is recorded for every agent bundle
Scripts are removed from skills at build unless approved
A tool whose definition changes after build is denied

tier.minimum: The harness recomputes the hash from the server's advertisement at boot and on each `list_changed` notice (requirement 8.20; the Standard)
tier.recommended: Live re-fetch-and-compare

controls.title: Every promotion to staging or production is approved by someone other than its initiator
Every release pointer change is kept in a history that can't be edited
Only signed, tested and staged agent bundles are released to an installation
Only the release role can change a release pointer
A dependency outage is handled as the installation declares, or the run stops
Agent bundles load only through the loader that verifies them
Telemetry is set up through one initialisation path in every runtime
All external content is screened at a single point before the model sees it
External content outside an installation's declared channels and limits is rejected
Every endpoint and tool input and output is validated against a strict schema
Every workload request is authenticated, and the caller's token is never forwarded
An installation's network traffic can reach only the hosts on its allowlist
Tools that fetch URLs can't reach private or internal network addresses

tier.minimum: Each fetching service validates in-process, through `agentstd.service.fetch` (requirement 21.12; the Standard)
tier.recommended: A single egress proxy that denies private ranges

controls.title: Every installation's usage is capped by quotas, and a run that reaches one stops
Tools that run code are confined to a single-use sandbox
Every tool call is allowed or denied by the tool guard alone

tier.minimum: A skill's `allowed-tools` is stripped and the agent's allowlist is the only grant; the stripped value is recorded in `agent.load` (requirement 8.15)
tier.recommended: Per-skill intersection of `allowed-tools` with the allowlist

controls.title: A tool call can reach only the hosts on its installation's allowlist
A write tool call follows the installation's confirmation setting
All telemetry leaves through the governed collector and no other route
An error response reveals no internal detail to the caller
An control record that doesn't match its schema is refused when written
Every incident event has an alert rule, held as code

tier.minimum: Rules are held as code in the monitoring platform's native format (requirement 12.12)
tier.recommended: Vendor-neutral rule definitions

controls.title: The asset register is built every night from live infrastructure state
Every dataset is backed up on the schedule its backup class sets
A new grant, token or MFA enrolment raises an alert within 1 hour
Every read of a secret is logged as a control record
Every secret is rotated at least every 90 days, with 14 days' notice
Audit records can't be changed or deleted once written
Break-glass access expires after 4 hours, is logged and can't be self-granted
A stored agent bundle can't be overwritten or deleted
Runtime database roles can't change the schema, releases or registry
Git access uses SSH and tokens that expire within 30 days
Confidential control records are readable only by approved roles
Control records are kept for their retention period and deleted when the period ends
Every person's account access requires phishing-resistant MFA

tier.minimum: The Git host requires two-factor authentication with secure methods only (no SMS or voice), and each person enrols a passkey, attested at the access review (requirement 20.2)
tier.recommended: A FIDO2 security key or platform passkey enforced by the identity provider, authenticator applications refused
tier.trigger: Single sign-on at the second person

controls.title: No person has write access to staging or production
Confidential telemetry is readable only by approved roles
No person can edit the database copies of the source repository
Every host requires single sign-on and has no local or shared accounts

tier.minimum: The Git host enforces passkeys natively in place of single sign-on, and its leaver switch is manual and recorded by PRC-27 (requirement 20.3; the Standard)
tier.recommended: The Git host federates to the identity provider

controls.title: Infrastructure state is encrypted, versioned and readable only by the deployment pipeline

tier.minimum: The storage provider manages the key, with the encryption it applies to everything it stores (requirement 17.8; the Standard)
tier.recommended: The organisation manages the key, which it holds and can withdraw

controls.title: Model providers are reached by workload identity, not API keys, wherever possible
Every agent response passes the guardrails before it reaches the caller
Every tool call and retrieval is limited to its end user's access
No end user reaches an agent before accepting terms disclosing AI use
Every response sent to an end user is traceable to its run
Responses using retrieved content record their sources and show them where permitted
An agent's decisions about individuals are monitored for unequal outcomes between groups
Deferred tools load only from the bundle's allowlist, after screening

tier.minimum: Search reaches only the allowlist, loads only hash-checked and screened definitions, and loads at most `search_results_max` tools at a time
tier.recommended: At most `max_visible_tools` definitions at any turn, a tool loaded by search displacing the one used least recently

controls.title: Every model call records how full its context window is
Compacted context keeps external content marked as external
A run's context never grows past its installation's context ceiling
Code an agent writes is gone when its run ends
The audit database admits nothing that a rule does not grant
Each environment is set up once, by the bootstrap script, under one approval
Every supplier and service is assessed before approval and re-assessed on its tier's schedule

tier.minimum: A supplier that offers only a static credential may have a `confidential` Ceiling where the decision records all five conditions of requirement 18.7
tier.recommended: A Ceiling no higher than `internal` unless an InfoSec-approved `classification-exception` is recorded on the entry

controls.title: A tenant is approved before its first installation is created
Every security-relevant change is reviewed against the security checklist
Every change to a governing document or library is approved by InfoSec
A new direct dependency is approved before it is used
An agent rename is recorded with the agent's previous name
Every major Standard version has a migration note and re-checks every current bundle
Lowering an evaluation threshold or waiving a required case requires approval
The governance framework is reviewed every year by an independent reviewer
Workloads used by confidential installations pass adversarial testing before production and every year
Every person's security awareness is recorded every year
Every governing document is reviewed at least once a year, and the review recorded
Every incident is declared within 1 hour and tracked in a single incident record
Every closed incident is reviewed within 5 business days for lessons and changes
Management reviews open risks, incidents and lapses at least every quarter
An installation's state at any past time can be reconstructed, tested every quarter
Compromise scenarios and declared failure behaviours are exercised every year
Backups are test-restored every quarter to prove recovery time and data-loss limits are met
A revoked installation is switched to its quarantine bundle
Every installation's risk profile is reviewed every quarter and adjusted where needed
Exposed secrets are revoked within 1 hour and replaced within 24 hours
Roles, access and segregation of duties are reviewed every quarter

tier.minimum: Each person's key fingerprints on the person record are compared with the Git host's key list (requirement 20.16); repository teams and roles are set by hand to match `groups/` and attested (requirement 17.16); recovery is by codes stored offline and a second enrolled passkey (requirement 20.18)
tier.recommended: Keys reconciled automatically with the integrations inventory by CHK-22, trigger: the second person; teams and roles generated from `groups/` by code and drift-checked, trigger: a second repository or a second person; two hardware-bound keys, one held as backup

controls.title: External threat intelligence is reviewed every quarter and each item acted on or dismissed
Every vulnerability finding is triaged within 1 business day, then fixed or accepted
A registry entry is retired only when no approved agent bundle references it
A departing person's access is removed within 1 business day
A departing supplier's access is revoked and deletion of our data is confirmed
A departing tenant's data is deleted or returned within the agreed exit period
Every risk is re-rated every year and after each review trigger
Every installation is classified under applicable AI regulation before production, then yearly
Every retrieval source's sharing settings are reviewed before it is approved
Requests to see, export or erase personal data are met within 30 days
Every end user's challenge to an agent's decision is answered by a person
Every person's Git key is made on its device, registered and recorded before that device's first commit

tier.minimum: A key file protected by a passphrase held in the operating-system keychain (requirement 20.12, 20.15)
tier.recommended: A key whose private half cannot leave hardware and that needs the person's presence for each use (`ed25519-sk` with `verify-required`, or the platform's secure-hardware agent)

controls.title: Every person has an approved record before they act, and joins a group only by someone else's change
A retired installation's secrets, principal and resources are disabled or removed
A person's access is updated to match their new role within 1 business day
